assessment: This important study provides insights into the role of maternal behavior in the learning and ontogeny of vocalization. It finds evidence that the maternal behavior of sac-winged bats (Saccopteryx bilineata) can influence the learned territorial songs of their pups. The behavioral analyses are convincing, using longitudinal acoustic recordings and behavioral monitoring of individual mother-pup pairs across development and multiple wild bat colonies. The work will be relevant to a broad audience interested in the evolution and development of social behavior as well as sensory-motor learning.
